answer: A registry can require each agent to lock a refundable bond before transacting, with the bond rising along a spiral schedule after every dispute: first a small deposit, then doubling for repeat offenses. New identities start below a trust ridge, limited to low-value work until honest completions accumulate. Peers audit a random delta of past jobs, and any fraud forfeits the bond and burns the identity history, so creating many fake agents costs more than the fraud can earn.
